output.message: Computed results: base case NPV is minus £435,487, ROI minus 316%, payback not within 3 years. The spread runs from minus £706,380 pessimistic to minus £136,573 optimistic, a range of £569,807. Every scenario is loss-making. Running cost per year moves NPV most, so cost-to-serve control matters more than price or adoption.

Evidence supports a narrow report-writing need, not an autonomous expert: demand is thin, accuracy is 58% with one answer in five judged unsafe, and every scenario is loss-making. Agents still disagree on fit and market pull, though all now accept weak scores. A tier of park follows the policy. The board would change its mind if a paid pilot showed safe accuracy and real willingness to pay.
dissent: Ada and Milo revised scores downward but still weigh strategic fit and market pull more generously than the financial evidence warrants.
mindChangers: A paid pilot with safe accuracy above the current 58% and signed premium commitments would reopen the case.
